source_text:
Πορευομένου μου εἰς Κώμας κατὰ τὸν καιρόν, ὃν καὶ πέρυσι, περιπατῶν ἀνεμνήσθην τῆς περυσινῆς ὁράσεως, καὶ πάλιν με αἵρει πνεῦμα καὶ ἀποφέρει εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον, ὅπου καὶ πέρυσι.
ἐλθὼν οὖν εἰς τὸν τόπον τιθῶ τὰ γόνατα καὶ ἠρξάμην προσεύχεσθαι τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ δοξάζειν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὄνομα, ὅτι με ἄξιον ἡγήσατο καὶ ἐγνώρισέν μοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου τὰς πρότερον.
μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς βλέπω ἀπέναντί μου τὴν πρεσβυτέραν, ἣν καὶ πέρυσιν ἑωράκειν, περιπατοῦσαν καὶ ἀναγινώσκουσαν βιβλαρίδιον, καὶ λέγει μοι: Δύνῃ ταῦτα τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναγγεῖλαι; λέγω αὐτῇ: Κυρία, τοσαῦτα μνημονεῦσαι οὐ δύναμαι: δὸς δέ μοι τὸ βιβλίδιον, ἵνα μεταγράψωμαι αὐτό. Λάβε, φησίν, καὶ ἀποδώσεις μοι.
ἔλαβον ἐγώ, καὶ εἴς τινα τόπον τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἀναχωρήσας μετεγραψάμην πάντα πρὸς γράμμα: οὐχ ηὕρισκον γὰρ τὰς συλλαβάς. τελέσαντος οὖν τὰ γράμματα τοῦ βιβλιδίου ἐξαίφνης ἡρπάγη μου ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τὸ βιβλίδιον: ὑπὸ τίνος δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.
Μετὰ δὲ δέκα καὶ πέντε ἡμέρας νηστεύσαντός μου καὶ πολλὰ ἐρωτήσαντος τὸν κύριον ἀπεκαλύφθη μοι ἡ γνῶσις τῆς γραφῆς. ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένα ταῦτα:
Τὸ σπέρμα σου, Ἑρμᾶ, ἠθέτησαν εἰς τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν εἰς τὸν κύριον καὶ προέδωκαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτῶν ἐν πονηρίᾳ μεγάλῃ καὶ ἤκουσαν προδόται γονέων καὶ προδόντες οὐκ ὠφελήθησαν, ἀλλὰ ἔτι προσέθηκαν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῶν τὰς ἀσελγείας καὶ συμφυρμοὺς πονηρίας, καὶ οὕτως ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι αὐτῶν.
ἀλλὰ γνώρισον ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα τοῖς τέκνοις σου πᾶσιν καὶ τῇ συμβίῳ σου τῇ μελλούσῃ ἀδελφῇ: καὶ γὰρ αὕτη οὐκ ἀπέχεται τῆς γλώσσης, ἐν ᾗ πονηρεύεται: ἀλλὰ ἀκούσασα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἀφέξεται καὶ ἕξει ἔλεος.
μετὰ τὸ γνωρίσαι σε ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῖς, ἃ ἐνετείλατό μοι ὁ δεσπότης ἵνα σοι ἀποκαλυφθῇ, τότε ἀφίενται αὐτοῖς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πᾶσαι, ἃς πρότερον ἥμαρτον, καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασιν μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας, ἐὰν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας μετανοήσωσιν καὶ ἄρωσιν ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν τὰς διψυχίας.
ὤμοσεν γὰρ ὁ δεσπότης κατὰ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν ὡρισμένης τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἔτι ἁμάρτησις γένηται, μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σωτηρίαν: ἡ γὰρ μετάνοια τοῖς δικαίοις ἔχει τέλος: πεπλήρωνται αἱ ἡμέραι μενανοίας πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις: καὶ τοῖς δὲ ἔθνεσιν μετάνοιά ἐστιν ἕως ἐσχάτης ἡμέρας.
ἐρεῖς οὖν τοῖς προηγουμένοις τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἵνα κατορθώσωνται τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν ἐκ πλήρους τὰς ἐπαγγελίας μετὰ πολλῆς δόξης.
ἐμμείνατε οὖν οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν δικαιοσύνην καὶ μὴ διψυχήσητε, ἵνα γένηται ὑμῶν ἡ πάροδος μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων. μακάριοι ὑμεῖς, ὅσοι ὑπομένετε τὴν θλῖψιν τὴν ἐρχομένην τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ὅσοι οὐκ ἀρνήσονται τὴν ζωὴν αὐτῶν.
ὤμοσεν γὰρ κύριος κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἀρνησαμένους τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτῶν ἀπεγνωρίσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς αὐτῶν, τοὺς νῦν μέλλοντας ἀρνεῖσθαι ταῖς ἐρχομέναις ἡμέραις: τοῖς δὲ πρότερον ἀρνησαμένοις, διὰ τὴν πολυσπλαγχνίαν ἵλεως ἐγένετο αὐτοῖς.
Σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μηκέτι μνησικακήσῃς τοῖς τέκνοις σου μηδὲ τὴν ἀδελφήν σου ἐάσῃς, ἵνα καθαρισθῶσιν ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. παιδευθήσονται γὰρ παιδείᾳ δικαίᾳ, ἐὰν σὺ μὴ μνησικακήσῃς αὐτοῖς. μνησικακία θάνατον κατεργάζεται. σὺ δέ, Ἑρμᾶ, μεγάλας θλίψεις ἔσχες ἰδιωτικὰς διὰ τὰς παραβάσεις τοῦ οἴκου σου, ὅτι οὐκ ἐμέλησέν σοι περὶ αὐτῶν: ἀλλὰ παρενεθυμήθης καὶ ταῖς πραγματείαις σου συνανεφύρης ταῖς πονηραῖς:
ἀλλὰ σώζει σε τὸ μὴ ἀποστῆναί σε ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος καὶ ἡ ἁπλότης σου καὶ ἡ πολλὴ ἐγκράτεια: ταῦτα σέσωκέν σε, ἐὰν ἐμμείνῃς, καὶ πάντας σώζει τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργαζομένους καὶ πορευομένους ἐν ἀκακίᾳ καὶ ἁπλότητι. οὗτοι κατισχύσουσιν πάσης πονηρίας καὶ παραμενοῦσιν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
μακάριοι πάντες οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν δικαιοσύνην. οὐ διαφθαρήσονται ἕως αἰῶνος.
ἐρεῖς δὲ Μαξίμῳ: Ἰδοῦ, θλῖψις ἔρχεται: ἐάν σοι φανῇ, πάλιν ἄρνησαι. Ἐγγὺς κύριος τοῖς ἐπιστρεφομένοις, ὡς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἐλδὰδ καὶ Μωδάτ, τοῖς προφητεύσασιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῷ λαῷ.
Ἀπεκαλύφθη δέ μοι, ἀδελφοί, κοιμωμένῳ ὑπὸ νεανίσκου εὐειδεστάτου λέγοντός μοι: Τὴν πρεσβυτέραν, παῤ ἧς ἔλαβες τὸ βιβλίδιον, τίνα δοκεῖς εἶναι; ἐγώ φημι: Τὴν Σίβυλλαν. Πλανᾶσαι, φησίν, οὐκ ἔστιν. Τίς οὖν ἐστιν; φημί. Ἡ Ἐκκλησία, φησίν. εἶπον αὐτῷ: Διατί οὖν πρεσβυτέρα; Ὅτι, φησίν, πάντων πρώτη ἐκτίσθη: διὰ τοῦτο πρεσβυτέρα: καὶ διὰ ταύτην ὁ κόσμος κατηρτίσθη.
μετέπειτα δὲ ὅρασιν εἶδον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου. ἦλθεν ἡ πρεσβυτέρα καὶ ἠρώτησέν με, εἰ ἤδη τὸ βιβλίον δέδωκα τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις. ἠρνησάμην δεδωκέναι. Καλῶς, φησίν, πεποίηκας: ἔχω γὰρ ῥήματα προσθεῖναι. ὅταν οὖν ἀποτελέσω τὰ ῥήματα πάντα, διὰ σοῦ γνωρισθήσεται τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς πᾶσιν.
γράψεις οὖν δύο βιβλαρίδια καὶ πέμψεις ἓν Κλήμεντι καὶ ἓν Γραπτῇ. πέμψει οὖν Κλήμης εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις, ἐκείνῳ γὰρ ἐπιτέτραπται: Γραπτὴ δὲ νουθετήσει τὰς χήρας καὶ τοὺς ὀρφανούς. σὺ δὲ ἀναγνώσῃ εἰς ταύτην τὴν πόλιν μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων τῶν προϊσταμένων τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
thought_title: The second vision: the little book, the sins of Hermas's house, and the identity of the old woman
orientation: A year after the first vision, the old woman gives Hermas a little book that warns his family and the whole church that the time for repentance is short. His wife is from now on to live with him as a sister, the book of Eldad and Modat is a lost book of prophecy, and Clement, Grapte and Maximus are fellow believers in Rome.
pass_a_gloss: While I was going to Cumae at the time, as also last year, walking I remembered the vision of last year, and again a spirit takes me up and carries me away to the same place, where also last year. Having come therefore to the place I put down my knees and began to pray to the Lord and to glorify his name, because he considered me worthy and made known to me my sins, the former ones. And after I rose from the prayer I see opposite me the old woman, whom also last year I had seen, walking and reading a little book, and she says to me: Can you announce these things to the elect of God? I say to her: Lady, so many things I cannot remember; but give me the little book, so that I may copy it. Take it, she says, and you will give it back to me. I took it, and having withdrawn to some place of the field I copied everything letter by letter; for I was not finding the syllables. When therefore I had finished the letters of the little book, suddenly the little book was snatched from my hand; but by whom I did not see. And after fifteen days, when I had fasted and asked the Lord many things, the knowledge of the writing was revealed to me. And these things were written: Your seed, Hermas, broke faith with God and blasphemed against the Lord and betrayed their parents in great wickedness and were called betrayers of parents, and having betrayed they were not helped, but still they added to their sins the licentious acts and the defilements of wickedness, and thus their lawless deeds were filled up. But make known these words to all your children and to your wife, the one who is to be a sister; for she also does not hold back her tongue, with which she does evil; but having heard these words she will hold back and will have mercy. After you make known these words to them, which the Master commanded to be revealed to you, then are forgiven them all the sins, which they formerly sinned, and to all the saints who have sinned until this day, if from the whole heart they repent and take away from their heart the double-mindednesses. For the Master swore by his glory upon his elect: if after this day has been fixed any sin still happens, they do not have salvation; for repentance for the righteous has an end; the days of repentance have been fulfilled for all the saints; and for the nations repentance is until the last day. You will say therefore to the leaders of the church, that they should make straight their ways in righteousness, that they may receive in full the promises with much glory. Remain therefore, you who work righteousness, and do not be double-minded, that your passing may be with the holy angels. Blessed are you, as many as endure the tribulation, the great one that is coming, and as many as will not deny their life. For the Lord swore by his Son, that those who have denied their Christ are disowned from their life, those who are about to deny in the coming days; but to those who denied formerly, because of his great compassion he became merciful to them. But you, Hermas, no longer hold a grudge against your children, nor let your sister go, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with a righteous discipline, if you do not hold a grudge against them. Grudge-holding works death. But you, Hermas, have had great private tribulations because of the transgressions of your house, because you did not care about them; but you were distracted and you were mixed up together with your evil business dealings. But what saves you is your not having departed from the living God and your simplicity and your great self-control; these things have saved you, if you remain, and they save all who work such things and walk in innocence and simplicity. These will prevail over all wickedness and will remain unto eternal life. Blessed are all who work righteousness. They will not be destroyed forever. And you will say to Maximus: Behold, tribulation is coming; if it seems good to you, deny again. The Lord is near to those who turn back, as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied in the desert to the people. And it was revealed to me, brothers, while I was sleeping, by a very handsome young man saying to me: The old woman, from whom you received the little book, who do you think she is? I say: The Sibyl. You are mistaken, he says, she is not. Who then is she? I say. The Church, he says. I said to him: Why then old? Because, he says, she was created first of all things; for this reason old; and for her sake the world was established. And afterward I saw a vision in my house. The old woman came and asked me, whether I had already given the book to the elders. I denied having given it. You have done well, she says; for I have words to add. When therefore I finish all the words, through you it will be made known to all the elect. You will write therefore two little books and you will send one to Clement and one to Grapte. Clement therefore will send to the cities outside, for to him it has been entrusted; and Grapte will admonish the widows and the orphans. But you will read in this city with the elders who preside over the church.

choices.why: The diminutive form is deliberate; the object is small enough to be held and copied by hand, and the diminutive recurs throughout the passage.
The phrase indicates copying exactly, character by character, which fits the following clause about not finding the syllables.
ἀθετέω with εἰς means to reject or set aside one's obligation toward someone; 'broke faith with' captures the covenantal force.
συμφυρμός is a mixing or defiling confusion; the genitive πονηρίας marks the source or character of the defilement.
κατεργάζομαι means to bring about or accomplish; the noun μνησικακία is rendered as a single concept to match the source's compactness.
The verb means to have one's thoughts drawn aside; the context contrasts caring for his household with being pulled away into business.

pass_b_english: I was on my way to Cumae, at the same season as the year before, and as I walked I remembered last year’s vision. And again a spirit took me up and carried me away to the same place as the year before.
So when I came to the place, I knelt down and began to pray to the Lord and to glorify his name, because he had counted me worthy and had made my former sins known to me.

When I rose from prayer, I saw in front of me the old woman I had seen the year before. She was walking and reading a little book. She said to me, “Can you report these things to the elect of God?” I said to her, “Lady, I cannot remember so much. But give me the little book, so that I may copy it.” “Take it,” she said, “and you shall give it back to me.”

I took it and went away to a place in the country, and I copied it all, letter by letter, for I could not make out the syllables. When I had finished the letters of the little book, suddenly the little book was snatched out of my hand. By whom, I did not see.
Fifteen days later, after I had fasted and asked the Lord earnestly, the meaning of the writing was revealed to me. This is what was written:

“Your offspring, Hermas, have broken faith with God. They have blasphemed the Lord and betrayed their parents in great wickedness. They have been called betrayers of parents, and their betrayal has gained them nothing. Instead they have added still more to their sins, wanton deeds and entanglements in wickedness, and so their lawless deeds have reached their full measure.

“But make these words known to all your children, and to your wife, who is to be your sister. For she too does not keep her tongue in check, and with it she does evil. But when she has heard these words, she will keep it in check, and she will find mercy.

“After you have made these words known to them, the words which the Master commanded me should be revealed to you, then all the sins they committed before are forgiven them. So it is for all the saints who have sinned up to this day, if they repent with all their heart and take double-mindedness out of their heart.

“For the Master has sworn by his glory concerning his elect: now that this day has been fixed, if there is any more sinning, they shall have no salvation. For repentance has an end for the righteous. The days of repentance are fulfilled for all the saints. But for the nations there is repentance until the last day.
“So you shall tell the leaders of the church to set their ways straight in righteousness, so that they may receive the promises in full, with great glory.

“Stand fast, then, you who work righteousness, and do not be double-minded, so that your passage may be with the holy angels. Blessed are you, all who endure the great tribulation that is coming, and all who will not deny their life.

“For the Lord has sworn by his Son that those who have denied their Christ have been rejected from their life, that is, those who are going to deny him now, in the days that are coming. But to those who denied him before, the Lord has been merciful, because of his great compassion.

“But you, Hermas, must no longer bear a grudge against your children, and you must not leave your sister to herself, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with a righteous discipline, if you bear no grudge against them. Bearing a grudge brings about death. And you, Hermas, have had great tribulations of your own because of the transgressions of your household, because you took no care for them. You paid them no heed, and you became entangled in your wicked business affairs.

“But what saves you is that you have not fallen away from the living God, and your simplicity, and your great self-control. These things have saved you, if you stand fast, and they save all who do such things and walk in innocence and simplicity. These will prevail over all wickedness and will endure to eternal life.
“Blessed are all who work righteousness. They shall never be destroyed.

“And you shall say to Maximus, ‘Look, tribulation is coming. If it seems good to you, deny again.’ ‘The Lord is near to those who turn to him,’ as it is written in the book of Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.”

Now, brothers, a revelation was given to me while I slept, by a very handsome young man. He said to me, “The old woman from whom you received the little book, who do you think she is?” I said, “The Sibyl.” “You are wrong,” he said. “She is not.” “Then who is she?” I asked. “The Church,” he said. I said to him, “Then why is she old?” “Because she was created first of all things,” he said. “That is why she is old. And for her sake the world was formed.”

Afterward I saw a vision in my house. The old woman came and asked me whether I had already given the book to the elders. I said that I had not. “You have done well,” she said, “for I have words to add. So when I have finished all the words, they will be made known through you to all the elect. You shall therefore write two little books, and send one to Clement and one to Grapte. Clement will send it to the cities abroad, for that has been entrusted to him. Grapte will admonish the widows and the orphans. And you shall read it in this city, together with the elders who preside over the church.”

problems.quote: If it seems good to you, deny again.
problems.why: The Greek is a conditional warning ('if it appears to you [that you must], deny again'), not a suggestion or permission ('if it seems good').
problems.fix: If it appears to you, deny again.

edits.old: If it seems good to you, deny again.
edits.new: If it appears to you, deny again.

problems.quote: If it appears to you, deny again.
problems.why: The imperative 'deny' is a mistranslation of the aorist subjunctive 'ἄρνησαι' (that you may deny), which expresses a purpose/result (so that you may deny), not a command.
problems.fix: If it appears to you, so that you may deny.

problems.quote: You were distracted and entangled yourself in your evil business dealings.
problems.source_quote: παρενεθυμήθης καὶ ταῖς πραγματείαις σου συνανεφύρης ταῖς πονηραῖς
problems.why: 'Entangled yourself' is a mistranslation of 'συνανεφύρης' (grew up with / were brought up with), which indicates a lifelong association or formation, not a temporary entanglement.
problems.fix: You were distracted and grew up with your evil business dealings.
problems.ruling: συνανεφύρης means 'were brought up with' (cf. LSJ), not 'entangled yourself'; translation loses the sense of lifelong formation with evil business.

edits.new: If it appears to you, so that you may deny.

edits.old: You were distracted and entangled yourself in your evil business dealings.
edits.new: You were distracted and grew up with your evil business dealings.

problems.quote: If it appears to you, so that you may deny.
problems.why: The source is a command ('deny again') or a warning of a repeated action, not a purpose clause ('so that you may deny').
problems.fix: If it appears to you, you will deny again.

problems.quote: If it appears to you, so that you may deny.
problems.why: πάλιν ἄρνησαι is a command 'deny again,' not purpose 'so that you may deny.'
problems.fix: If it appears to you, do not deny again.
problems.ruling: Greek ἐάν σοι φανῇ, πάλιν ἄρνησαι is a conditional command ('if it appears, deny again'), not a purpose clause 'so that you may deny'.

problems.why: Inconsistent capitalization makes it unclear when 'church' is the allegorical woman/institution vs. generic.
problems.fix: Capitalize consistently when referring to the allegorical Church.

problems.why: These terms overlap but are not identical; reader cannot tell if 'elect' = 'saints' or if distinctions exist.
problems.fix: Add note that 'elect' and 'saints' are largely synonymous in this text.

problems.quote: your wife who is about to become your sister
problems.why: Implies future celibacy or spiritual sibling relationship; 'sister' was early Christian marital language but jarring here.
problems.fix: Footnote: 'sister' was common Christian address, here implying spiritual reconciliation.

problems.quote: as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness
problems.why: Cited as Scripture but not in any canonical Bible; is extracanonical.
problems.fix: Note: non-canonical source, possibly from lost Jewish-Christian tradition.

problems.quote: an ivory bench lying there, and on the bench lay a linen cushion
problems.why: The same piece of visionary furniture is called 'chair,' 'bench,' and 'seat' across sections.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'chair' or 'throne' throughout.

problems.quote: as it is written in Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness
problems.why: This is presented as Scripture but refers to a lost apocryphal work, not a canonical book.
problems.fix: Note that Eldad and Modat is an apocryphal text, not canonical Scripture.

fixed: Capitalization of 'church': The English uses 'the church' in the phrase 'the leaders of the church' and 'the elders who lead the church.' The source has τῆς ἐκκλησίας, referring to the Church as the institution/community. The brief's glossary lists 'ἐκκλησία' as 'church' with the sense 'the Church, pre-existent and created first.' The English is lowercase in these instances, which is inconsistent with the allegorical Church. However, the confirmed problem says 'Inconsistent capitalization makes it unclear when church is the allegorical woman/institution vs. generic.' In the English, 'the church' appears only in these two places, both referring to the same institution. The source does not distinguish between allegorical and generic; it is always the Church. The brief's glossary entry is lowercase 'church' but the sense is capitalized 'the Church.' The English should capitalize 'Church' when referring to the institution. I will edit 'the church' to 'the Church' in both places.

The elect vs. saints: The confirmed problem says 'These terms overlap but are not identical; reader cannot tell if elect = saints or if distinctions exist.' The source uses ἐκλεκτοῖς and ἁγίοις. The English uses 'the elect' and 'the saints.' The brief's glossary has 'ἐκλεκτοί' as 'the elect' and no entry for 'saints.' The source does not explicitly equate them, but they refer to the same group of faithful. The English is accurate. No edit needed.

Mistranslation of 'your wife who is about to become your sister': The source is τῇ συμβίῳ σου τῇ μελλούσῃ ἀδελφῇ. The literal gloss is 'your wife, the one who is to be a sister.' The English 'your wife who is about to become your sister' implies a future change in status. The source uses μέλλουσα, which can mean 'about to be' or 'destined to be.' The brief's glossary does not cover this. The confirmed problem says 'Implies future celibacy or spiritual sibling relationship; sister was early Christian marital language but jarring here.' The English is a literal rendering of μέλλουσα. However, the source does not imply celibacy; it is a spiritual relationship. The English 'about to become' is a bit misleading. The literal gloss 'the one who is to be a sister' is better. I will change 'about to become' to 'to be' to match the source more closely.

Wrong scripture: Eldad and Modat. The source is ὡς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἐλδὰδ καὶ Μωδάτ. The English 'as it is written in Eldad and Modat' is accurate. The confirmed problem says 'Cited as Scripture but not in any canonical Bible; is extracanonical.' The brief's names section lists 'Ἐλδὰδ καὶ Μωδάτ' as 'Eldad and Modat.' The English is correct. No edit needed.

last_rejected.quote: If it appears to you, deny again.
last_rejected.why: The imperative 'deny' is a mistranslation of the aorist subjunctive 'ἄρνησαι' (that you may deny), which expresses the danger of falling away, not a command to do so.
last_rejected.fix: If it appears to you, you may deny again.
last_rejected.ruling: ἄρνησαι is 2nd aorist subjunctive, but in a conditional clause it can function as an imperative; the translation is defensible and not a major error.
